key_concepts: Momentum is the product of mass and velocity
Momentum and velocity are vector quantities
The unit of momentum is kg·m/s
An isolated system has no external forces such as friction or air resistance
The law of conservation of momentum states total momentum before collision equals total mo
For objects that stick together after collision, m1v1 + m2v2 = (m1 + m2)v′
During collision, objects exert equal and opposite forces on each other
Objects with different masses accelerate differently during collision
Momentum is conserved in all collisions
Marble collisions demonstrate transfer of momentum through a line of marbles
